name: Cline
official_status_notes: Autonomous open-source coding agent; published as IDE extension, SDK, CLI, and desktop app (verified Sep 2026).
pricing_summary: Open source; brings your own keys or uses paid plans/provider keys as configured.
best_for: VS Code users who want a fully transparent, BYOK, MCP-connected coding agent.
strengths: Open source (Apache-2.0), deep BYOK/local support, MCP, plan/act modes, human-in-the-loop file+terminal approvals.
weaknesses: Requires you to manage your own API keys/costs; deep agentic work consumes tokens quickly.
hardware_requirements: Lightweight editor extension; any API-based model works on low-end hardware.

name: Kilo Code
official_status_notes: Open-source AI coding agent (MIT). Site confirms acquisition by Anaconda in 2026; IDE (VS Code/JetBrains), CLI and cloud agents.
pricing_summary: Free BYOK agent with model routing (Efficient/Frontier/Free) and subscription plans.
best_for: Students and developers who want a free, open-source VS Code agent with many model options and no markup.
strengths: MIT license, 500+ models via gateway, BYOK, local models, MCP, agent modes (Code/Architect/Debug), CLI + cloud agents.
weaknesses: Fast-moving project; docs and pricing must be re-checked often.
hardware_requirements: Any machine that runs VS Code.

name: Continue
official_status_notes: GitHub repo is read-only as of Sep 2026; final 2.0.0 release covers the CLI, VS Code extension, and JetBrains plugin (Apache-2.0, freely available as a foundation). The registry also records the acquisition by Cursor (Anysphere) per the official site â€” verify there for transition guidance.
pricing_summary: Open-source BYOK; hosted hub has free tier; subscription discontinued after acquisition.
best_for: Learning how BYOK/local-model IDE assistants work; forks and the OSS codebase.
strengths: Transparent OSS, deep BYOK/local model support, MCP, VS Code/JetBrains.
weaknesses: Future development is now primarily within Cursor, not the standalone product.

name: GitHub Copilot
official_status_notes: Active. Free tier, Pro, Pro+, Business, Enterprise plans; VS Code, JetBrains, Visual Studio, CLI, mobile; agent mode; MCP support in IDE/CLI (verified docs Sep 2026).
pricing_summary: Free tier exists; paid tiers add models/agent features. Includes CLI and cloud agent.
best_for: GitHub-centric developers who want integrated autocomplete + chat + agents in one subscription.
strengths: Tight GitHub integration, fast autocomplete, chat, agent mode, CLI, mobile app, wide IDE support.
weaknesses: Closed source; no BYOK; model choice limited to Copilot's catalog.

name: Gemini Code Assist
official_status_notes: Google's Gemini-powered IDE assistant (VS Code + JetBrains) with a free tier for individuals. Verify current quota/plan details on the official site.
pricing_summary: Free tier; enterprise tier via Google Cloud.
best_for: Gemini users who want a no-cost IDE assistant for personal projects.
strengths: Free tier, strong Gemini models, chat + completions, some agentic features.
weaknesses: Less transparent BYOK; confusion with Gemini CLI feature set.

name: Cursor
official_status_notes: Active AI IDE; site states 'Cursor is now a part of SpaceX' (Aug 2026). Verify ownership status before citing.
pricing_summary: Free Hobby tier; Pro subscription; BYOK possible for some models.
best_for: Developers who want a polished agentic IDE with very good codebase understanding.
strengths: Tab autocomplete, Cmd-K inline edits, agent mode, background agents, multi-model choice (Claude/GPT/Gemini/Grok), MCP.
weaknesses: Closed source; pricing subject to change; heavy usage binds you to their subscription.

name: Windsurf
official_status_notes: Cognition announced acquisition of Windsurf on 2025-07-14 (official blog, verified). Windsurf continued operating as a product under Cognition; Devin (Cognition's autonomous agent) integrates with Windsurf. Check windsurf.com for current state.
pricing_summary: Free tier; subscription plans.
best_for: Developers who like a Cursor-style agentic IDE with a strong Cascade/agent model.
strengths: Agentic 'Cascade', good context engine, MCP, IDE focus.
weaknesses: Closed source; ownership changed twice in ~18 months (Codeium to Windsurf to Cognition).

name: Void
official_status_notes: Open-source VS Code fork; BYOK and private-LLM focused; Chat/Agent/Gather modes (verified Sep 2026).
pricing_summary: Free, open source, BYOK.
best_for: Developers who want an open-source Cursor-like editor with BYOK/local privacy.
strengths: Open source, direct-to-provider (no private backend), local + frontier models, checkpoints for LLM changes.
weaknesses: Younger ecosystem; fewer enterprise features.
hardware_requirements: Runs on modest Windows machines; cloud inference for models.

name: PearAI
official_status_notes: Open-source AI IDE fork with an agent. The previously recorded repository no longer resolves (404, verified Sep 2026); verify the project's current state before relying on it.
pricing_summary: Free (BYOK) at last check.
best_for: Experimenting with open-source agent IDE forks.
strengths: Open source; Cursor-like experience with BYOK.
weaknesses: Small team; feature velocity uncertain.

name: Sixth
official_status_notes: Not verified â€” check official documentation before using.
pricing_summary: Unknown
best_for: Unknown
strengths: Unknown
weaknesses: Unknown

name: Augment Code
official_status_notes: Agentic development platform with Context Engine, Cosmos orchestration, CLI; oriented at org-scale SDLC (verified Sep 2026).
pricing_summary: Commercial; paid plan (pricing page).
best_for: Teams that want code-review, incident, ticket-to-PR automation agents.
strengths: Context engine, cosmo orchestration, code review and security-remediation loops.
weaknesses: Enterprise-oriented; not a student/budget tool.

name: Tabnine
official_status_notes: Acquired by Tricentis (announced on official site, verified Sep 2026). Enterprise AI coding platform angle; on-prem/air-gapped options.
pricing_summary: Free tier; Pro; Enterprise.
best_for: Enterprises needing on-prem/air-gapped code assistance.
strengths: Multiple model support, on-prem deployment, context-aware completions, style learning.
weaknesses: Not open source; agentic capability varies by tier.
hardware_requirements: Cloud or on-prem server; client is lightweight.

name: Sourcegraph Cody
official_status_notes: Sourcegraph deprecated Cody for individual users (mid-2025); it remains available in Sourcegraph Enterprise. Check Sourcegraph for current guidance.
pricing_summary: Enterprise offering; individual free tier removed.
best_for: Enterprise Sourcegraph customers.
strengths: Code Search integration, chat + auto-edit, context from remote repos.
weaknesses: No longer a consumer tool; enterprise-only now.

name: Roo Code
official_status_notes: GitHub archived the Roo-Code repo on May 15, 2026. Extension shut down May 15, 2026. Fork 'ZooCode' (community) and Cline (origin) recommended as alternatives per archived README.
pricing_summary: Was free/BYOK with paid API options.
best_for: Learning from its design; evaluating forks like ZooCode.
strengths: Powerful modes (Code/Architect/Ask/Debug), MCP, strong community, Cline fork lineage.
weaknesses: Archived/product shut down May 2026 â€” not an active recommendation.

name: Twinny
official_status_notes: Actively developed; MIT license; local-first completion/chat extension (verified Sep 2026).
pricing_summary: Free, open source, BYOK/local.
best_for: Local-model (Ollama) chat and FIM completion in VS Code at zero cost.
strengths: MIT license, local-first, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, workspace embeddings.
weaknesses: Not an autonomous agent; completion/chat focus.
hardware_requirements: Runs well; local models need RAM for larger sizes.

name: Supermaven
official_status_notes: Fast autocomplete with 1M-token context; free tier and Pro plans (verified Sep 2026).
pricing_summary: Free tier; Pro from ~$10/mo.
best_for: Fast inline completions with very large context.
strengths: Latency, 1M context, style adaptation.
weaknesses: Autocomplete/chat only; no autonomous agent.

name: Qodo
official_status_notes: Open-source PR-Agent / Qodo Merge components under qodo-ai; commercial products (Qodo Merge pro, Qodo Gen) are proprietary.
pricing_summary: Credit-based pro plans; free for open source projects.
best_for: Automated PR code review and quality gating.
strengths: PR review, rules engine, cross-repo context, IDE plans.
weaknesses: Review-focused, not a general coding agent.

name: Refact.ai
official_status_notes: Open-source personal + enterprise AI coding agent; self-hosted option; cloud shutting down (site notice, verified Sep 2026).
pricing_summary: Free tier; Pro from $10/mo; Enterprise on-prem.
best_for: Developers who want an autonomous agent that can be self-hosted.
strengths: Autonomous agent, fine-tuning option, on-prem/air-gapped, RAG, completions.
weaknesses: Cloud service winding down; self-host path is the main route.
hardware_requirements: Client is lightweight; self-hosting needs its own server.

name: JetBrains Junie
official_status_notes: BYOK coding agent for JetBrains IDEs, CLI, GitHub/GitLab actions; AI credits or BYOK pricing (verified Sep 2026).
pricing_summary: Free to start with 5 AI credits; BYOK zero-markup; AI Pro/AI Ultimate subscriptions.
best_for: JetBrains users who want an in-IDE agent with BYOK.
strengths: Runs in JetBrains IDEs, planning mode (plans in .junie/plans), live prompting, human-in-the-loop review.
weaknesses: JetBrains-ecosystem oriented; CLI experience younger.

name: Zed AI
official_status_notes: Zed editor (Rust-written, open source) with AI/agent features; AI features include billing tiers (verified Sep 2026).
pricing_summary: Editor free; AI assistant has paid subscription; BYOK varies.
best_for: Performance-focused developers open to switching editors.
strengths: Native-speed editor, built-in agent, collaboration, open source.
weaknesses: Editor switch required; AI plans are subscription-based.
hardware_requirements: Very light; good for 8 GB machines.

name: Firebase Studio
official_status_notes: Google announced sunset of Firebase Studio effective March 22, 2027; no new workspaces. Migration suggested to Google AI Studio / Google Antigravity (banner verified Sep 2026).
pricing_summary: Free during preview; Google Developer Program grants extra workspaces.
best_for: Rapid full-stack app prototyping in the browser while it remains available (until Mar 2027).
strengths: Full-stack agent (App Prototyping), Gemini AI, preview + Android emulator, deploy via App Hosting.
weaknesses: Being sunset (March 22, 2027).

name: Amazon Kiro
official_status_notes: Proprietary AWS IDE (spec-driven development). Not open source; verify current availability/pricing on the official site.
pricing_summary: Free tier; credit-based paid plans.
best_for: Developers who want a spec-first, plan-heavy agent workflow with a full IDE.
strengths: Spec-driven development, property-based tests, parallel agents, open source, AWS-hosted.
weaknesses: New-ish product; feature velocity fast but young.
hardware_requirements: IDE is Code OSS based; lightweight.

name: Trae
official_status_notes: Free AI IDE (VS Code fork) with plug-in ecosystem; supported models vary by region. Verify current details.
pricing_summary: Free tier; premium features later.
best_for: Free Cursor alternative if available in your region.
strengths: Free, integrates many models, agent workflow.
weaknesses: Closed source; regional availability and data handling to verify.

name: Aide
official_status_notes: Aide.dev site (Sep 2026) frames the project as a developer-tools research lab; SWE-bench blog posts remain. Verify active maintenance before relying on it.
pricing_summary: Unknown
best_for: Unknown
strengths: Research reputation: SWE-bench work (scaling test-time inference).
weaknesses: Product status uncertain.

name: Amazon Bedrock IDE
official_status_notes: Bedrock-managed models surface through IDE integrations (VS Code / JetBrains + Amazon Q Developer). Verify availability per region.
pricing_summary: AWS usage-based pricing via Bedrock model invocation.
best_for: Teams standardized on AWS Bedrock models.
strengths: Enterprise governance, many models via one gateway.
weaknesses: Not a consumer tool; developer experience is auxiliary to AWS.

name: GitLab Duo
official_status_notes: GitLab Duo is a proprietary product feature. GitLab the platform is open-core, which does not make Duo open source.
pricing_summary: Required Premium/Ultimate plan additions; credit-based usage.
best_for: GitLab-hosted teams wanting AI across MR/issue/CI lifecycle.
strengths: Deep GitLab integration, agent platform, governance, model selection.
weaknesses: Requires GitLab subscription; not a standalone tool.

name: IBM watsonx Code Assistant
official_status_notes: IBM's AI coding agent is now branded 'IBM Bob' (Bob-Shell CLI, IDE modes Ask/Plan/Agent; pricing from $20/instance, verified Sep 2026). watsonx is the underlying enterprise AI stack.
pricing_summary: AWS usage-based pricing via Bedrock model invocation.
best_for: IBM mainframe/hybrid modernization projects.
strengths: Legacy modernization (COBOL->Java/C++), governance, agentic modes.
weaknesses: Enterprise-only angle; premium pricing.

name: Codeium
official_status_notes: Codeium was renamed to Windsurf in 2024-2025; product continues under the Windsurf brand.
pricing_summary: Free tier; paid plans under Windsurf brand.
best_for: Historical; users should evaluate Windsurf.
strengths: Fast completions, chat, some agent features.
weaknesses: Rebranded into Windsurf; treat Codeium name as legacy.

name: Amazon Q Developer
official_status_notes: AWS agentic coding assistant (successor to CodeWhisperer); VS Code/JetBrains extensions plus the Amazon Q CLI. Verify current AWS pricing tiers before use.
pricing_summary: Free tier for individual use plus paid Pro tier â€” verify the current limits on AWS pricing.
best_for: Developers already in the AWS ecosystem who want an IDE agent with AWS-aware guidance.
strengths: Deep AWS integration, IDE + CLI + agent workflows, free tier.
weaknesses: Proprietary; value drops sharply outside AWS projects; limits change.
hardware_requirements: Runs with VS Code or JetBrains IDEs.

name: Theia IDE
official_status_notes: AI-native open-source cloud & desktop IDE built on the Eclipse Theia platform â€” an open alternative to VS Code (not a fork, but compatible with the VS Code extension ecosystem via Open VSX); BYOK to any provider incl. self-hosted/local models; no telemetry (verified Sep 2026).
license: EPL-2.0 (platform; GPL-2.0 with classpath exception option)
pricing_summary: Free, open source; model costs follow the provider you connect.
best_for: Privacy-conscious developers and organizations wanting an open, vendor-neutral IDE with AI agents and full model control.
strengths: Open governance (Eclipse); BYOK to any provider or local models; VS Code extension compatibility; cloud + desktop.
weaknesses: Smaller community than VS Code; some extensions work better in VS Code proper.
hardware_requirements: Comparable to VS Code; light for cloud models.

name: CodeGeeX
official_status_notes: Open multilingual code model (CodeGeeX4-ALL-9B, GLM lineage) plus official VS Code/JetBrains extensions; a local-mode deployment guide connects the extensions to a self-hosted model. Code under Apache-2.0; model weights under a separate Model License (commercial use requires registration) (verified Sep 2026).
pricing_summary: Free extension; self-hosted model on your own hardware; check commercial terms for the weights.
best_for: Open-weight autocomplete/code assistant you can self-host for privacy or research.
strengths: Strong small-model benchmark results; local mode; VS Code + JetBrains.
weaknesses: Weights license restricts commercial use; less polish than commercial assistants.
hardware_requirements: 9B model self-hosting wants ~16 GB RAM; cloud extension mode is light.
